Dynamic Task Manager process descriptions

EXE: DWAgent-dynamic-10443-v5-x64.exe
Portal: https://82.25.46.70:10443/
Config: os_win_installer/install-dynamic-10443-v5.json
SHA256: 23613de2f62fbcc2e833b35f910aefe1a54d0602364bca0c8e7ad3acf5e15e2c

Set Service display name in the existing portal to the desired friendly name,
for example Remo Dw. This value controls both installed EXEs' FileDescription
and ProductName, the Windows service display name, and the Control Panel name.
Executable filenames retain .exe; Windows service name remains a separate
internal identifier. Main and service filenames can both be RemoDw.exe because
they are installed in different folders. Publisher remains a separate setting.

Names are read from the existing authenticated server profile during setup.
There is no new portal field, server deployment or port change. The new flag
dynamic_process_description enables this only in this new installer config.
Saving a portal change affects new installations or verified replacements;
already installed processes retain their existing profile until reinstalled.
Task Manager determines process grouping. Its Details tab shows actual filenames.

Only copied installation executables receive metadata changes, before startup.
Updates are staged beside each EXE and atomically replaced after success;
write/commit/replace failures preserve the original copy and stop installation.
Fixed versions, existing version strings, copyright, company metadata, executable
code, icons and manifests are preserved. Missing version strings derive from the
fixed version so Windows and .NET readers recognize the new description.
Changing executable resources removes the source runtime's valid Authenticode
signature. The customized Python copy was confirmed NotSigned; it was not signed
as any portal Publisher. Code signing/UAC publisher is a separate mechanism.

Validation: 123 installer tests and 16 portal identity/client credential tests
passed, including eight real Windows process-description integration tests.
Independent version.dll and .NET FileVersionInfo reads confirmed both labels.
Both customized runtime and native service executables passed harmless execution
checks on temporary copies. No agent service was installed, started or stopped.
Payload archive integrity, source/native equality, default-only installer profile,
Python 3.8 syntax and preservation of all 72 pre-existing EXEs were verified.
The portal and its existing services/ports were not modified.
